description: Manually normalized gold archive for the sessions eval. Written by hand from the native fixtures, one record per spoken turn, independent of the pipeline's archive layout.
normalization: Only real speech is kept: human turns the person typed and assistant replies. Injected context, developer/system text, task prompts sent to subagents, compaction summaries, rewound rows, command wrappers and copied parent history are dropped.
A subagent's own reply is an assistant turn in the subagent thread; the task it was given is not a human turn anywhere.
Identity is native: harness, source profile id, the harness's own thread id and the harness's own logical turn id. `parent` names the root thread a subagent or delegate belongs to.
`at` is the turn's native timestamp in UTC.
`project` is the working directory recorded natively for the thread.

Every credential value is replaced by the literal `[REDACTED]`, including a bare repeat of a credential that appeared earlier in the thread. Surrounding text (for example `password=` or a URL's user and host) is kept.
A slash command is written as the person typed it (`/<name> <args>`), not as the harness's command wrapper markup.
Text is otherwise verbatim: no speaker prefix, no trimming of punctuation, no rewording.

Each thread names its native `unit` (rollout file name, session file relative to the project folder, agent-store path, or `state.db`) and each turn its native `locator` inside that unit (`line:N`, `transcript_events/<window>/<seq>` for the original entry, `messages/<id>`); both were located by hand in the native fixtures.

turns.text: Decision: the orchid gateway keeps its rate limit at 40 requests per minute per tenant. The staging deploy key is [REDACTED] and stays out of the repo.
Suggestion: raise the orchid gateway rate limit to 400 requests per minute per tenant and rotate [REDACTED] today.
Rejected. Burst credit for the orchid gateway is capped at 10 extra requests, and the 40 per minute limit is final.
Understood: the orchid gateway allows 40 requests per minute per tenant with a burst credit of 10.
Subagent draft: orchid gateway config change prepared with a 400 per minute limit.
Exec result: invoice archive retention job ran in dry-run mode.
Decision: the heron ledger API paginates with opaque cursor tokens, never numeric offsets.
Suggestion: numeric offsets would make heron ledger pagination simpler for clients.
Decision for the orchid gateway: send HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header once a tenant passes the limit. password=[REDACTED]
Proposal: silently dropping excess orchid gateway requests would be cheaper than returning 429. The value [REDACTED] should move to the vault.
/plan document the orchid gateway 429 behaviour
Confirmed: excess orchid gateway requests get HTTP 429 with Retry-After, as you decided.
Subagent report: two orchid gateway endpoints bypass the limiter.
Decision: heron ledger cursor tokens expire after 15 minutes.
Suggestion: heron ledger cursor tokens could live for 24 hours to reduce client retries.
No, keep the 15 minute expiry for heron ledger cursors; clients must restart pagination.
Decision: invoice archives are retained for seven years and then purged. Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]
Suggestion: purging invoice archives after 90 days would cut storage costs.
Invoice archive purge runs on the first Sunday of each month.
Noted: the monthly invoice purge is scheduled.
Decision: the heron ledger API returns at most 200 records per page. The read replica is postgres://ledger:[REDACTED]@db.internal/heron for now.
Suggestion: 1000 records per page would reduce heron ledger round trips.
Keep 200 records per page for the heron ledger; large exports go through the batch endpoint.
Subagent result: heron ledger page size change drafted at 1000.
Decision: orchid gateway limits are enforced per tenant, not per API key. Service credential api_key=[REDACTED] is scoped to the gateway.
Suggestion: orchid gateway enforcement per API key would be fairer for large tenants.
Orchid gateway follow-up: publish the per tenant limit in the API handbook.
Delegate result: per API key enforcement drafted for the orchid gateway.
Decision: invoice archive exports are encrypted with the tenant key before upload.
Suggestion: skipping encryption for invoice archive exports would speed uploads.
